newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN approves $610 mln Gulf War Kuwaiti damage claim.
newsitem.headline: UN approves $610 mln Gulf War Kuwaiti damage claim.

text.p: The Gulf War reparations body on Tuesday approved a $610 million damage claim filed by Kuwait Oil Company against Iraq for oil well fires started by Baghdad's fleeing troops, U.N. officials said.

The Governing Council of the United Nations Compensation Commission, composed of the same 15 members as the Security Council, also agreed with a judges' panel which said another $340 million of the Kuwaiti claim should be deferred. The oroginal claim was for a total of $950 million.
"It has been approved. The result is $610 million," Carlos Alzamora, executive secretary of the Geneva-based fund, told reporters.
KOC, a subsidiary of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation, filed its claim for $950 million in July 1993.
This is the first corporate claim approved by the body established by the Security Council in 1991 to set compensation for damage caused during Iraq's invasion and seven-month occupation of Kuwait.

KOC said Iraqi troops, fleeing a Western coalition led by the United States, set 800 oil wellheads ablaze. Some 27 firefighting teams from 10 countries including the United States and Kuwait, took months to extinguish the fires.
